title: Where is the patient? ED-to-ward location visibility for Inpatient Pharmacy
source: Poster (The Problem / Why It Matters / Proposed Solution / Our Objective) + director's brief v3

lines.text: Where is the patient?
A patient is admitted, and planned for the ward.
Admitted? Yes.
Still in the Emergency Department? Maybe.
lines.speak: Still in the Emergency Department? ... Maybe.

lines.text: Already in the ward? Maybe.
That uncertainty is the problem.
The problem isn't the admission.
It's knowing where the admitted patient actually is.
Inpatient Pharmacy needs to know one simple thing:
is the patient still in ED, or already in the ward?
Every time the answer isn't immediately visible, someone has to ask.
And Pharmacy's work depends on that answer.
So what if the system itself could make that transition clearer?
Here is an initial proposal.
While the patient is still in ED, register them in PHIS at Kecemasan & Trauma (Admission).
That location would mean: still at the ED admission stage.
When the patient physically enters the ward, the location would be updated to the actual ward.
But this is only an initial proposal. It must be validated, clinically and technically —
including whether this is the correct PHIS mechanism.

scenes.name: How the location would be updated

lines.text: Under this initial proposal, the location would be updated in eight steps.
In Visit Management, select Kecemasan & Trauma (Admission), and find the patient.
Open the patient's visit, and click Edit.
In the Transfer Detail List, select the new ward location, and save.
The location would then move from ED admission to the ward.
